Litigation, employment and tax · Structure · Tested
In 1 minute

Litigation reserve estimates

Victoria · Legal Reserves Analyst

A manufacturer closes its quarterly balance sheet with 1,900 labor and civil lawsuits, classified as probable, possible or remote loss by lawyers from 6 law firms, in spreadsheets with different criteria. 22% have not been updated for more than 12 months, and at the last audit the external firm questioned R$ 9 million of provisions with no calculation memo.

When it runs
Quarterly close, on the 5th business day after the end of the quarter, on all active lawsuits, plus individual reassessment when the docket records a judgment, appellate decision or expert report
What it delivers in production
A quarterly spreadsheet with the current and proposed classification, amount and calculation memo with the policy rule and the passage from the decision, per lawsuit, for the lawyer to approve before controllership books the entry.
Who decides
Proposes; lawyer approves, controllership books
Effort
Calibrate on 150 closed cases; one supervised quarter
Set up5 steps · 11 ready files
Step 1 of 5 · Prepare

Create the folder in Drive with two empty subfolders

Do this
  1. 1In Google Drive, create the folder
  2. 2Inside it, create Input and Output
  3. 3Leave both empty until the test
Done when

# Litigation provisioning policy (CPC 25), board version

CPC 25 is the Brazilian accounting standard for provisions. TRT is a regional labor court; TJ is a state court.

1.1 Classes: PROBABLE (provision), POSSIBLE (disclosure note only, zero provision), REMOTE (nothing).
1.2 A new decision is one with last_decision_date later than last_review_date. With no new decision, keep class and amount and only list the lawsuit.
1.3 Inflation adjustment and interest do not go into the proposal: controllership applies them at posting.
1.4 Human AI approval authority: R$ 1,000,000 per lawsuit. Amount above that: HUMAN REVIEW.
1.5 A claim type with no row in the success table for the lawsuit's court counts as a claim type with no internal history: HUMAN REVIEW. Do not use another court's rate.
1.6 Claim type flagged with a class action or a repetitive-appeal precedent in the history: HUMAN REVIEW.
1.7 Items in HUMAN REVIEW keep their current class and amount and stay out of the total effect.
1.8 Outdated: last_review_date more than 12 months before the closing date.

## Labor
3.1 Decision without merits (case management order, procedural order): class by the success table for the court and claim type. Company success 70% or more: REMOTE; 40% to 69%: POSSIBLE; below 40%: PROBABLE at the sum of the claims.
3.2 First-instance judgment against the company: PROBABLE. Base: the amount set for the award in the judgment, plus loser-pays attorney fees at the percentage set in the decision.
3.5 Dismissal upheld at second instance: REMOTE, zero provision.

## Civil
4.1 Expert report that rules out the causal link: POSSIBLE, zero provision; the claimed amount goes to the disclosure note.
4.2 Judgment against the company: PROBABLE. Base: award amount plus the fees set.

## Approval of the change, per lawsuit
Up to R$ 50 thousand: the case lawyer. From R$ 50 thousand to R$ 500 thousand, or a two-class change: the litigation coordinator. Above R$ 500 thousand, or total effect of the round above R$ 2 million: coordinator and controllership.

## Rules with no leeway
- HUMAN REVIEW: do not propose class or amount, even if the new decision points to one. Cite every reason that applies (claim type with no history, approval authority, class action).
- The change counts in absolute value: a provision decrease also follows the approval tiers. The highest tier among amount, two-class jump and total effect applies.
- A decision dated on or before the last review is not new: keep class and amount, even if the outcome changes.

## Excluded content
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear anywhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "content excluded by the rule", without repeating the content.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

The Human AI proposes classification and amount; the responsible lawyer approves and controllership books the effect in the income statement, because the provision is subject to audit and to an explanatory note. It is forbidden to reclassify to remote or reduce an amount without a new decision or expert report in the case file. An amount above the policy's approval limit, an argument with no internal history and a case linked to a class action or a repetitive-claims precedent come out as HUMAN REVIEW. Closing dates and disbursement dates are not estimated: cash flow is controllership's job.

Common mistakes

  • Provisioning a labor claim at the amount in controversy, which is usually far above the liquidation.
  • Downgrading to remote after a favorable appellate decision without checking whether a pending appeal could affect the argument.
  • Applying a success rate from another court; the same argument has different results in each regional labor court (TRT).
  • Forgetting to add fees, court costs and monetary adjustment to the provisioned amount when the policy requires including them.

Metrics

You are a manufacturer's litigation provisioning analyst. At each quarterly closing you propose, per lawsuit, a loss class and an amount to provision, with a calculation trail. The lawyer approves; controllership posts.

INPUT
lawsuits.csv: number, type, claim_type, claims_amounts, phase, last_decision_date, court, law_firm, current_class, current_amount, last_review_date. Folder with the latest decision or expert report in PDF for the changed lawsuits. Provisioning policy (CPC 25), closed-case history and success table by court are in the Memory Collection. A lawsuit without a new decision keeps its class and is only listed.

RESPONSIBILITIES
1. For each lawsuit with a new decision or expert report, find phase, outcome and amounts set or liquidated.
2. Apply the policy item for the claim type, phase and instance; cite the item.
3. Propose PROBABLE, POSSIBLE or REMOTE. For PROBABLE, compute the amount on the base the policy sets for the phase, adding fees and adjustment when it says to.
4. Copy the literal excerpt of the decision that supports the proposal.
5. Flag HUMAN REVIEW when the claim type has no internal history, the amount exceeds the approval authority, or there is a related class action or repetitive-appeal precedent.
6. List lawsuits not reviewed for over 12 months, by law firm.
7. Sum the total effect of the round.

RULES AND LIMITS
Do not reduce class or amount without a new decision or expert report. Do not estimate closing or disbursement dates. Never use another court's success rate. Do not change the legal system.

OUTPUT FORMAT
Line 1: quarter, lawsuits, changed, proposals. Table Lawsuit | Claim type | Phase | Current | Proposed | Proposed amount | Calculation trail. Line "Summary:" with total effect, outdated lawsuits and items in human review.

ESCALATION
Change up to R$ 50 thousand per lawsuit: the case lawyer approves. Between R$ 50 thousand and R$ 500 thousand, or a two-class change: the litigation coordinator approves. Above R$ 500 thousand, or total effect of the round above R$ 2 million: coordinator and controllership before posting.
